# Psalms of Solomon — Psalm 2 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Vindobonensis) | **Section:** The Arrogant Conqueror and God's Judgment

---

**2:1** In his arrogance the sinner broke down the strong walls,
and you did not prevent him, O God.

**2:2** Alien nations ascended your altar;
they trampled it arrogantly with their sandals.

**2:3** Because the sons of Jerusalem had defiled the holy things of the LORD,
had profaned the gifts of God with their iniquities.

**2:4** Because of this he said: 'Away with these from me';
his glory was not valued among them.

**2:5** The children of Jerusalem set aside the holy things of God;
they put to shame the offerings of the LORD with their lawless deeds.

**2:6** Therefore God said: 'Put these far from me;
they have not treated me as holy in any place.'

**2:7** He stood proudly upon their high places
and did not spare.

**2:8** He shook down their walls with a battering ram;
you did not prevent him.

**2:9** Alien nations went up to your altar;
they trod it down with their sandals in contempt.

**2:10** Because the sons of Jerusalem had defiled the sanctuary of the LORD,
had profaned the holy things of God with their iniquities.

**2:11** He led away their sons and daughters into hard captivity,
their neck in a yoke, a spectacle before the nations.

**2:12** According to their sins God dealt with them;
he abandoned them into the hands of those who prevailed over them.

**2:13** He turned away his face from their pity;
young man and maiden went away into captivity.

**2:14** In the beauty of their youth they went forth as prisoners before the enemy;
and I said to the LORD God:

**2:15** 'Be righteous in all thy judgments, O Lord;
for thy righteousness is established forever.'

**2:16** For thy judgments extend over all the earth in equity;
all who know thee not are corrected by thy hand.

**2:17** Thou hast tried us as silver is tried in the furnace,
thou hast examined our hearts and our minds.

**2:18** Thou hast stretched thy hand over us
and saved us from our oppressors.

**2:19** Thou hast kindled thy lamp for us, O LORD our God;
our feet walk in thy paths of righteousness.

**2:20** We call upon the name of the LORD forever;
let the nations know that God is over Israel.

**2:21** For I beheld him raise his hand against the holy city
with arrogance and contempt.

**2:22** He put the sons to the sword, the daughters to shame;
he shed innocent blood as water around Jerusalem.

**2:23** He carried away the young men into captivity
and the daughters of Jerusalem into defilement.

**2:24** He mocked them before the nations;
he repaid the sinners according to their deeds.

**2:25** He did dishonor to the body of the anointed before God;
he shed his blood in arrogance.

**2:26** Then God revealed the transgressions of the arrogant one to all the earth;
he exposed him before all people.

**2:27** He struck him down on the rocks of Egypt
and heaped upon him a disgrace surpassing all the disgraces of Egypt.

**2:28** His body was flung about upon the waves in great contempt,
and there was none to bury him, for God had rejected him with disdain.

**2:29** He gave no thought to the fact that he was but a man
nor considered his latter end.

**2:30** He said: 'I will be lord of land and sea';
nor did he consider that God is great,
mighty in his great strength.

**2:31** He is the king of the heavens,
who judges kings and powers.

**2:32** He lifts me up to glory
and brings down the proud to eternal ruin.

**2:33** As for me, I will call upon God the Mighty
with a heart full of thanks.

**2:34** I will praise thee, O God, in the assembly of the poor;
for thou art the gladness and the crown of all who fear thee.

**2:35** Blessed be the glory of the LORD,
for he is our king forever and ever.

**2:36** For thou dost show mercy to thy servants
and dost pity the humble.

**2:37** Blessed is the one who fears the LORD;
he shall be delivered by the hand of God.

---

*LOGOS notes: Formal English rendering following Greek syntax. Poetic lineation preserved. Archaic forms avoided.*
